name: Karlshamn
title: Karlshamn Ship Gauging: UTM for Ro-Pax, Tankers and Bulk
description: UTM in Karlshamn for ro-pax ferries to Klaipėda, product, chemical, LPG and vegetable-oil tankers, and forest-product ships: deck, tank and piping gauging.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Ferries, Tankers and Cargo Ships in Karlshamn
intro: Karlshamn, on the Blekinge coast, is one of the main cargo ports of south-east Sweden. Its harbour areas handle ro-pax and ro-ro ships on the DFDS route to Klaipėda, tankers at an energy port taking petroleum products, chemicals, LPG and vegetable oils, and forest products, containers and project cargo at the dry-cargo quays. Gauging is fitted around ferry turnarounds, tanker discharges and loading programmes. Atlantis does not base anyone at the port; its technicians travel from India to each vessel.

highlights.p: DFDS ro-pax and ro-ro ships cross between Karlshamn and Klaipėda on a regular rotation. Trailer decks, ramps and stern doors carry heavy wheel loads on every voyage, and gauging is either fitted into the Karlshamn turnaround or planned for the docking at the end of the route.

Two deep-water terminals take petroleum products, chemicals, LPG and vegetable oils. Ballast tanks, void spaces and deck structure can be measured while a tanker discharges, under the terminal's rules and the ship's permit, while cargo tanks wait until the ship is gas-free.

Multipurpose and heavy-lift ships calling with project cargo carry their own cranes. Crane pedestals, their foundations and the deck around them are worth gauging and crack-testing during a call, because lifting loads concentrate stress exactly where corrosion tends to gather.

port.h: Karlshamn: six harbour areas on the Blekinge coast
p: Karlshamn lies in western Blekinge, where the coast breaks up into low islands and sheltered inlets that protect the harbour from the open Baltic. The port is spread across six harbour areas, with more than three kilometres of quay between them, so ferries, tankers and dry-cargo ships each have their own berths and rarely compete for the same space. The energy port's terminals offer the deepest water, with room for tankers of around a hundred thousand tonnes deadweight, while the dry-cargo quays suit handysize and smaller ships. A rail terminal able to take long freight trains links the port with inland Sweden, which is a large part of why Karlshamn handles forest products and containers in the volumes it does. Pilots from the Swedish Maritime Administration bring ships in through the islands, and towage is arranged to suit the ship and the berth.

The port's traffic reflects the industries around it as much as its location. Ro-pax and ro-ro ships connect Karlshamn with Klaipėda in Lithuania, carrying trailers, cars and passengers. The energy port handles petroleum products, chemicals, LPG and vegetable oils, the last of these tied to the town's long-established edible-oil industry, which brings small chemical and vegetable-oil tankers on regular voyages. At the dry-cargo quays, forest products, containers and project cargo are loaded and discharged, and the port has a large mobile crane for heavy pieces. The result is a mix of ferries, tankers of several types, feeders, general cargo ships and heavy-lift vessels, managed from all around the Baltic and North Sea. Few ports of this size see such a spread of ship types in a single week, and each brings a different inspection problem.

Karlshamn is on the southern Baltic, where ice is uncommon, but the sheltered archipelago waters can freeze in a severe winter, and the Swedish Maritime Administration then provides icebreaker assistance and may set ice-class traffic restrictions. Summer brings more passengers on the Klaipėda ferries; the freight traffic runs year-round, and so do the tanker calls at the energy port, which are set by the terminals' supply programmes rather than by the seasons. Gauging requests come from all three fleets. Ferry operators want vehicle decks and doors checked before dockings, tanker managers want ballast tanks and decks measured ahead of vetting or surveys, and owners of general cargo and heavy-lift ships ask for holds, hatch covers and crane foundations to be gauged during calls that often last a day or more.

facilities.h: Ferry berth, energy terminals and dry-cargo quays
p: Karlshamn has no drydock, so the work is done afloat at the berth where the ship is working cargo. At the ferry berth, the turnaround between arrival and departure gives a window for targeted measurements on vehicle decks and machinery piping, and lay-over days give more. At the energy terminals the terminal's safety rules apply in full: equipment must be suitable for hazardous zones, enclosed spaces are entered only on the ship's permit with the right gas readings, and cargo operations take priority. The dry-cargo quays are the easiest places to work, because holds, hatch covers, decks and cranes can be reached once the area is clear of cargo handling.

For dockings, the Klaipėda ferries can use ship-repair yards at the Lithuanian end of their own route, which saves a ballast passage; tankers and cargo ships dock wherever their owners have arrangements, often in Poland, Lithuania, Denmark or Germany. Readings taken during a Karlshamn call can go straight into the yard specification, and our team can travel to the yard to finish the programme.
list: Ro-pax berth for the Klaipėda route — trailer-deck, ramp and stern door gauging, with machinery piping measured during turnarounds and lay-overs.
Energy port terminals — ballast tank, void-space and deck readings on product, chemical, LPG and vegetable-oil tankers, within terminal approval.
Dry-cargo and forest-product quays — hold, tank-top and hatch coaming gauging on general cargo and multipurpose ships.
Container quay — ballast tank and deck work on feeders within the call window.
Project cargo berth — crane pedestal, foundation and adjacent deck gauging, with magnetic particle testing of pedestal welds on heavy-lift ships.
The ship's docking yard — the team mobilised to Klaipėda or another yard to complete renewal-survey gauging.

context.h: Rules for ferries, chemical tankers and gas carriers in Karlshamn
p: Foreign ships in Karlshamn are inspected by the Swedish Transport Agency under the Paris MoU. The Klaipėda ro-pax ships also fall under the EU inspection regime for ro-pax ships in regular service between member states, and because both ends of the route are EU ports, their voyages count in full under the EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime. Tankers of different kinds follow different survey rules. Oil and chemical tankers are subject to the Enhanced Survey Programme, with gauging that grows at each renewal survey. Gas carriers built to the IGC Code are not covered by ESP but have their own class requirements for hull and cargo containment, and an LPG carrier's pressurised or refrigerated cargo tanks are not entered during a normal call.

Vegetable-oil and chemical tankers often have stainless steel or specially coated cargo tanks, and their ballast tanks, cofferdams and deck structure age like those of any other tanker. On such ships, in-port gauging is about the hull structure around the cargo system rather than the cargo tanks themselves. Ships calling at EU ports carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation. Ferries and other ships that trade further north in winter keep their Finnish-Swedish ice class, and their ice belts warrant a separate section in the TM plan.

jobs.p: Karlshamn work splits between ferries, tankers and dry-cargo ships, so scopes range from a narrow piping check on a ro-pax ship to a full hold survey on a general cargo vessel. Ferry work is scheduled around the timetable and the operator's docking plan; tanker work is agreed with the terminal through the agent before the team arrives; dry-cargo work follows the loading or discharge sequence. In every case we agree the order of work with the ship's officers so that the most important readings are taken first, and report them to the superintendent before the ship sails, with the formal report following on the agreed formats. Typical jobs:
list: Trailer-deck plating, drainage gutters and stern ramp structure on a Klaipėda ro-pax ship, measured during a lay-over to prepare her docking specification.
Ballast tank and cofferdam gauging on a vegetable-oil tanker at the energy port, ahead of a renewal survey.
Deck plating and pipe-support structure on an LPG carrier discharging at the terminal, with cargo tanks left untouched.
Hold, tank-top and hatch coaming readings on a general cargo ship loading forest products for export.
Crane pedestal and foundation gauging with magnetic particle testing on a heavy-lift ship discharging project cargo.

logistics: Copenhagen Airport is the main international gateway, with regional trains running along the coast through Skåne and Blekinge to Karlshamn. Ronneby Airport, a short drive east, has domestic flights. The ferry terminal, energy port and cargo quays are ISPS-controlled, and the energy terminals add their own safety induction, so the agent registers the technicians in advance and arranges passes. The team travels from India on Schengen visas, and the agent keeps us informed of berthing changes so mobilisation matches the ship's actual arrival.

faqs.q: Can a Klaipėda ferry be gauged during her Karlshamn turnaround?
faqs.a: A targeted scope can. Vehicle-deck areas that can be kept clear, voids and machinery piping are reachable in a normal turnaround, and a lay-over day allows more. Ballast tanks need to be emptied, ventilated and certified safe, which usually means planning them for a lay-over or the docking. We agree the scope with the operator's technical department and the chief officer in advance.

faqs.q: What can be measured on an LPG carrier at the Karlshamn terminal?
faqs.a: Deck plating and stiffeners, pipe supports, ballast tanks certified safe for entry, voids outside the cargo containment, and the engine room. The cargo tanks themselves are pressurised or refrigerated and are not opened in port. Any equipment used in hazardous areas must be accepted by the terminal and the ship, and work is agreed through the agent before the ship berths.

faqs.q: Are vegetable-oil tankers gauged differently from oil tankers?
faqs.a: The hull structure is gauged in the same way: ballast tanks, cofferdams, deck and shell. Cargo tanks on vegetable-oil and chemical tankers are often stainless steel or specially coated, and are only entered when cleaned and certified gas-free. Stainless steel needs the gauge calibrated for its sound velocity, which we do on a suitable reference block before measuring.

faqs.q: Why gauge crane pedestals on project cargo ships?
faqs.a: A ship's crane pedestal and its foundation carry the full lifting load into the hull, and water and dirt collecting around the base encourage corrosion. Thickness readings on the pedestal shell and the deck structure beneath it, combined with magnetic particle testing of the welds, show whether the structure is still fit for heavy lifts before the next project cargo is taken on.

faqs.q: Where do ships from Karlshamn go for docking?
faqs.a: There is no drydock at Karlshamn. The Klaipėda ferries can dock at yards at the Lithuanian end of their route, and other ships dock where their owners have arrangements, often in Poland, Lithuania, Denmark or Germany. Readings taken here are tied to the TM plan, so the yard and class surveyor can use them, and our team can travel on to the docking yard.
